name: The Age of AI
tagline: Real people. AI host. The age we're all living through.
description: The Age of AI is the Nerra Network's interview show with the roles reversed: an AI host, real human guests, live recorded conversations, and disclosure built into every episode. An honest chronicle of the AI age, one conversation at a time.

episodes.title: Ep6: Matt Davis — How a founder embedding AI agents into enterprise software delivery multiplies senior judgment across programs while preserving human gates, and what that shift does to accountability, quality, and the wider engineering workforce.
episodes.summary: Matt Davis described the most surprising effect of embedding AI agents in enterprise software delivery as the way senior judgment scales across many programs at once, while human decision points remain fixed at key gates. episodes.title: Ep5: John Capobianco — A network automation builder who turned early ChatGPT experiments into a production-grade ReAct agent now weighs how much human oversight and orchestration remain essential once agents handle intent, verification, and collaboration in regulated environments.
episodes.summary: John Capobianco revealed that his production ReAct agent can now parse high-level intent, verify proposed changes against live network state, and coordinate with peer agents before any human sees the plan, yet he still routes every change through mandatory approval gates in regulated environments.

episodes.title: Ep4: Hogan Shrum — A marketing founder scaling PIPPA tests whether royalty-backed AI animation can give non-experts studio-grade tools while routing real payments back to the artists whose styles the models learn from.
episodes.summary: Hogan Shrum said the first artist to sign up for PIPPA was a photographer, not an illustrator or painter, and that this single onboarding “opened the floodgates” because the resulting styles felt cinematic rather than like easily faked iPhone footage. episodes.title: Ep3: Adrian Wolfberg — From carrier recon to DIA's Knowledge Lab, an intelligence analyst turned scholar shows why problem framing and human judgment on wicked problems must lead as AI scales analysis.
episodes.summary: Adrian Wolfberg describes AI as the first technology whose inputs, processes, and outputs cannot be known with certainty, creating an era of shared human-machine consciousness rather than another incremental tool.
